originalText:
claude fable 5 acaba de hacer posible publicar 100 videos UGC de IA por día en 4 plataformas en SOLO 30 minutos de producción

todo lo demás funciona 100% de forma autónoma

los clippers podrían estar acabados 

este modelo mythos observa material de video crudo y encuentra momentos virales que los transcritos pasarían por alto

navega por tiktok mientras duermes y crea informes de tendencias, generando 100 paquetes de producción y renderizándolos a través de higgsfield MCP sin que toques otra pestaña.

así que documenté la MÁQUINA ENTERA con cada prompt, cada instrucción de configuración y cada paso del flujo de trabajo

aquí está lo que hay dentro:

→ el sistema de investigación de mercado nocturno que funciona mientras duermes

(cowork navega por 5 plataformas, analiza 60-80 piezas de contenido cada una, devuelve un informe de inteligencia de tendencias con 10 ideas de contenido específicas para cuando te despiertes)

→ identificación de clips de píxeles crudos que encuentra momentos que los clippers humanos pasan por alto

(cambios en expresiones faciales, revelaciones de productos, picos de lenguaje corporal, incongruencias visuales. todo con marca de tiempo y clasificado por virabilidad predicha.)

→ generación de scripts en lote y activos: 20 paquetes de producción completos por prompt, ejecutado 5 veces para un total de 100

(scripts de 6 tomas, prompts de personajes, prompts de fotogramas de productos, dirección de voz, subtítulos para plataformas. 15-25 minutos en total.)

→ el pipeline de higgsfield MCP que renderiza los 100 videos automáticamente

(fable 5 llama directamente a seedance 2.0. referencia de personaje bloqueada. sincronización de labios alineada. cero intervención humana.)

→ el predictor de viralidad que filtra tus 20 mejores candidatos antes de publicar

(puntuación de gancho, tasa de retención, activación de regiones cerebrales. los 5 peores se diagnostican y revisan automáticamente.)

→ la matemática del CPM: 400 publicaciones en plataformas/día × 3,000 vistas promedio = 36M vistas/mes = $180k/mes a $5 CPM

→ los 6 prompts de copiar y pegar que ejecutan toda la máquina

todo basado en mi experiencia personal al ver detrás de escenas cómo Rizz App + Looksmax AI + Memix escalaron más allá de 7 cifras con este méto

originalText:
Someone prompted Claude Fable 5 to generate the entire journey of a baby developing in the womb. It built a fully explorable, first-person 3D world. In a browser. From a single prompt.

Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's first publicly available Mythos-class model, released June 9, 2026. You describe a world in plain language. It builds the whole thing, with full 3D rendering, playable directly in your browser.

This is the same model that rendered Borges's "Library of Babel" as a 3D game where you pull books off infinite shelves and climb spiral staircases. The same model that built a to-scale Yosemite Valley with 266,000 individually placed trees using real NASA elevation data, all in a single session.

On Anthropic's senior engineer benchmark, Fable 5 scored 91/100. The previous flagship scored 63.

Now someone walked through the womb.

We are not building apps anymore. We are building worlds.

#AI #ClaudeFable5 #Anthropic

note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
Feels obligatory to test Claude Fable 5’s performance in game development.

I fed it an old rougelike HTML action game I previously built with Opus, and Fable 5 turned it into 3D in 10 minutes.

The upgrade is obvious

- Animation
Before: Nano Banana + motion frame generator + ASCII converter to get usable action sprites and animation.
After: prompt directly generates the weapon and matched animation.

- Audio Design
Before: only one basic hit sound repeated.
After: BGM, hit SFX, enemy kill SFX, and level clear audio.

- Visual
Before: ASCII visuals were mostly flat and hard to push into action gameplay.
After: it preserved the 2D ASCII aesthetic, while adding 3D depth, perspective, and impact through a hybrid rendering style.

- Character
Before: even simple boss designs like a spider or tiger were hard to recreate.
After: it pulled boss prototypes from my design doc, turned them into 3D models, and animated them in one pass.

The attacks also feel much better, though I’m not 100% sure how much of that comes from my earlier stat tweaks versus Fable itself.

This is the real intent-to-gameplay moment.

title: Autonomous agent workflow for Fable 5
author: RetroChainer
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
Claude Fable 5 shipped today. The model isn't the lecture. The metric is.

Anthropic tracks one number for Claude: time horizon how long an agent stays coherent on a single goal before drifting.

Claude Opus 4 could build a feature. Six months ago: an overnight run. 

Fable 5: days on one goal, per the keynote.

The practical part nobody writes down:

Keep your dead prototypes. The ones that almost worked. Re-run them on every Claude release. 

They're your private eval for the exponential.

Most teams test the new Claude on tasks that already worked. That measures nothing.

When a broken prototype flips to working that's the signal. Ship that week.

The capability didn't arrive. It was scheduled. Your prototypes are the calendar.
